A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Verification Learning study. All pages, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix A report original recognition experiments on Addition, Sort, Match and Chess, together with runtime comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: Section 7 retains the original recognition experiments, runtime comparisons and ablations, with all five result tables now in the main text.

M1.justification: The verification framework, DCS search, scoring alternatives, distribution alignment and test-time correction are retained. Section 4.1 explicitly adds insertion of each selected assignment's successors into the heap, clarifying v1's existing description of tracking successors of every verified assignment rather than establishing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Addition with bases 2–10, Sort with sequence lengths 4–8, Match with 6–10 character categories, and Chess with 2–6 piece types. No evaluated dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding table. WSABL is renamed A3BL, but both versions cite He et al. (2024) and report identical results for this comparator. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported architecture, optimizer, learning rate, task configurations and testing procedures remain unchanged. V2 newly states a common ten-epoch training budget; v1 specifies no conflicting budget, so this is additional disclosure rather than evidence of a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same independent versus non-independent scoring comparisons and with/without test-time-correction ablations. Moving Sort and Match tables from the appendix introduces no new ablation, robustness test or supplementary empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetition counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The theoretical probability bounds are not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and timeout/memory-limit outcomes match. V1 Tables 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 correspond respectively to v2 Tables 1, 5, 4, 2 and 3. The additional runtime-scaling discussion concerns these unchanged results.

T1.justification: V2 adds Appendix A proofs for previously unproved Theorems 4.1, 4.2 and 6.1. It also introduces Theorem 4.4 and its proof, asserting that score monotonicity is necessary and sufficient for general sub-exponential COP solving. This substantially expands the theoretical content.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes optimal ordered search and low search-management overhead. V2's conclusion explicitly claims proven sub-exponential COP solvability under independence or monotonicity, supported by the new Theorem 4.4. This substantially strengthens the central computational guarantee, while retaining the original unsupervised-learning contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 strengthens the characterization of non-monotone optimization without exhaustive search from 'difficult' to 'impossible.' Section 7.5 additionally interprets the unchanged runtimes as showing relatively slow growth with symbol-space size. The symmetry-based limitations and distribution-alignment rationale remain.

D1.justification: V2 discloses the common ten-epoch budget, clarifies that recognition tables report symbol accuracy, and makes the DCS successor-insertion step explicit. Appendix B's verification code and the stated code-access location are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references covering semantic and algorithmic supervision, self-explanation and recent abductive learning. Notably, the introduction now identifies DCS as an extension of Jia et al. (2025). The overall related-work taxonomy and positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: V2 locally revises the abstract, introduction, algorithm explanation and conclusion; splits Section 6 into knowledge-induced and data-induced error subsections; and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds two substantial explanatory diagrams: the supervised/unsupervised comparison and the VL training workflow. It also moves the Sort and Match tables into the main text, consolidates all four accuracy tables on one page, and clarifies captions. These materially change the visual organization despite unchanged results.

improvement.justification: The diagrams, proof appendix and ten-epoch disclosure improve accessibility and documentation. However, the new Theorem 4.4 and conclusion assert sub-exponential COP solving without establishing it: Appendix A.3 invokes ordered successor generation, while Section 4.1's runtime still depends on the unrestricted rank K of the first feasible assignment. The documentation gains therefore coexist with a substantial new unsupported guarantee, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
